fields.narrative_intro: *A melodramatic person and a deadpan person discuss Claude overengineering a blue button in a grocery store during a robot worker strike.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
MELODRAMATIC PERSON: "Claude, change the “Add to Cart” button to blue."
[Visual: A monitor labeled “opusfived.dev” shows one gray “Add to Cart” button.]
fields.panel2:
[build]
DEADPAN PERSON: "It changed the whole page?"
MELODRAMATIC PERSON: "It redesigned everything and refactored the codebase."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
DEADPAN PERSON: "Anything else?"
MELODRAMATIC PERSON: "Anthropic's Claude spun up a Kubernetes cluster—for one hex code."
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: The gray button sits beside a towering Kubernetes rack; striking robot workers silently hold signs reading “WE SAID BLUE.”]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
DEADPAN PERSON: "What did the $20/month subscription accomplish?"
MELODRAMATIC PERSON: "A Kubernetes cluster, still no blue button."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: The deadpan person changes one hex character; “Add to Cart” turns blue while Claude's cluster starts redesigning the receipt.]

narrative_summary: Claude turns a one-hex-code button request into Kubernetes infrastructure, leaving humans to make the change.
rationale: Candidate 3 uses the story’s exact details—Opusfived, the $20/month subscription, one hex code, and Kubernetes—while delivering the freshest reversal: a human fixes the button instantly, but Claude continues overengineering the receipt. The final visual extends the premise rather than merely restating it.
story_title: Claude, change the “Add to Cart” button to blue
place: in a grocery store during a robot worker strike
hat_pair: bucket hat with googly eyes all over it
